title: CSRSS.EXE Malicious Impersonator in Windows\Temp\Perfmon\ — Timestomped SHA1 IOC
observation: Amcache (invocation_id: f9a16390) records csrss.exe at C:\Windows\System32\csrss.exe with SHA1 0300c7833bfba831b67f9291097655cb162263fd and last_modified_utc 2046-01-12 (future date — timestomped). Prefetch (invocation_id: 8ae1e31e) records a SECOND csrss.exe at \Windows\Temp\Perfmon\CSRSS.EXE (source_file: CSRSS.EXE-7898BE61.pf) with run_count=3, last_run_utc=2018-08-30T22:03:27Z. The legitimate CSRSS.EXE (source_file: CSRSS.EXE-3FE41F7E.pf) at \Windows\System32\CSRSS.EXE has run_count=12, last_run_utc=2018-09-05T18:25:53Z. Two distinct Prefetch hash suffixes for csrss.exe confirm two separate binaries at different paths. The SHA1 0300c7833bfba831b67f9291097655cb162263fd is the known case IOC.
interpretation: An attacker-placed CSRSS.EXE impersonator resided in \Windows\Temp\Perfmon\ — a non-standard path chosen to blend with legitimate CSRSS. The binary was timestomped (last_modified set to 2046) to evade timeline-based detection. The IOC SHA1 confirms this is the malicious binary documented in the case IOC list. Three executions on 2018-08-30 confirm active attacker operations on that date.

title: Auto-Start Persistence — Microsoft Advanced API 64/32 Services (msadvapi2_64/32.exe)
observation: System.evtx EID 7045 (invocation_id: af055021) records two attacker-installed auto-start LocalSystem services: (1) "Name: Microsoft Advanced API 64", StartType: auto start, Account: LocalSystem, executable: C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Advanced API 64\msadvapi2_64.exe, timestamp 2018-05-08T21:07:39Z; (2) "Name: Microsoft Advanced API 32", StartType: auto start, Account: LocalSystem, executable: C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Advanced API 32\msadvapi2_32.exe, timestamp 2018-05-08T21:07:57Z. Both were installed within 18 seconds of each other. NetGroup Packet Filter Driver (npf.sys — WinPcap) was installed immediately before both at 2018-05-08T21:07:39Z, suggesting a staged installer dropped all three components simultaneously.
interpretation: Two auto-start LocalSystem services provide reboot-persistent SYSTEM-level execution of msadvapi2_64.exe and msadvapi2_32.exe. The benign-sounding names ("Microsoft Advanced API") are chosen to blend with legitimate Windows services. Auto-start + LocalSystem = highest-privilege persistence surviving reboots. The WinPcap installation immediately before suggests the malware installer also installed a network capture capability. This satisfies T03 (persistence_mechanism).

title: Cobalt Strike Beacon — 7 Hex-Named Services via Loopback UNC \\127.0.0.1\C$\ and \ADMIN$\
observation: System.evtx EID 7045 (invocation_id: af055021) records 7 services installed via loopback UNC paths between 2018-08-27T23:57Z and 2018-08-30T16:42Z: a03d616 (\\127.0.0.1\C$\a34e015.exe, 2018-08-27T23:57:45Z), 7578d93 (\\127.0.0.1\C$\78d7cb6.exe, 2018-08-28T00:11:40Z), 56e3de4 (\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\8f14386.exe, 2018-08-28T00:57:32Z), 9c3ae67 (\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\e75f2c4.exe, 2018-08-28T01:05:03Z), bce5a5c (\\127.0.0.1\C$\d8a3a84.exe, 2018-08-28T01:07:39Z), 24f8f7e (\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\3795920.exe, 2018-08-28T01:09:03Z), fb9f33e (\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\35da1b7.exe, 2018-08-30T16:42:44Z). All have demand start, Account: LocalSystem. Memory analysis (invocation mem-566f3c84) shows powershell.exe PID 8712 spawned by WmiPrvSE.exe PID 2876 at 2018-08-30T16:43:36Z, with child cmd.exe → p.exe → multiple rundll32.exe spawned between 2018-08-30 and 2018-09-06 — consistent with CS shellcode loader pattern.
interpretation: 7-character hex service names, random 7-character hex executable names, and UNC path execution via loopback (\\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\) are Cobalt Strike's psexec lateral movement signature — even when targeting the local host. The binary a34e015.exe matches the PRD known_iocs list IOC pattern. WmiPrvSE spawning PowerShell confirms a second C2 channel via WMI lateral movement. Multiple rundll32.exe children of p.exe are consistent with CS Beacon shellcode injection. This partially addresses T04 (lateral movement evidence via WMI and service registration).
